```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>",
  eval = requireNamespace("org.Hs.eg.db", quietly = TRUE)
)
library(rsemverse)
```

`rsem_read()` makes a handful of decisions on your behalf. This page lists them
in the order they happen, with the reason for each. The demonstrations query
`org.Hs.eg.db` directly, so you can see the facts the rules are based on.

## 1. The input is checked before anything is read

The function stops, without returning a partial result, if:

* `data` is not a folder or `metadata` is not a file;
* `metadata` lacks the column `sample_id` or `ref`, has no rows, has an empty or
  duplicated `sample_id`, or lists the same file twice;
* a listed file does not exist in `data`;
* a file lacks `gene_id` or the column that `expr` selects, has non-numeric or
  missing values, or has a duplicated `gene_id`;
* the files do not contain the same genes in the same order.

The last rule matters because the function stacks the files column by column.
If sample B listed its genes in another order, the numbers would silently
belong to the wrong genes. See [Troubleshooting](troubleshooting.html) for the
messages.

Only the columns `gene_id` and the one you chose (`expected_count` or `TPM`)
are read. Other columns, such as `FPKM`, `length` or the posterior columns of
newer RSEM versions, are ignored.

## 2. The species must match the IDs

The function looks at how many gene IDs start with `ENSG` (human) or `ENSMUSG`
(mouse). If your `species` disagrees, it stops. If the IDs are neither (for
example, if RSEM was run on a reference that names genes by symbol), it stops
as well, because there is nothing to look up.

## 3. Versions are removed before the lookup

RSEM names genes with Ensembl IDs that carry a version, such as
`ENSG00000141510.18`. The OrgDb packages use the ID without the version. The
difference is not cosmetic: with the version the lookup finds nothing.

```{r}
suppressMessages(library(org.Hs.eg.db))
lookup <- function(ids) {
  r <- suppressMessages(AnnotationDbi::select(
    org.Hs.eg.db, keys = ids, keytype = "ENSEMBL", columns = "SYMBOL"
  ))
  setNames(r$SYMBOL[match(ids, r$ENSEMBL)], ids)
}
lookup(c("ENSG00000141510.18", "ENSG00000141510"))
```

So `rsem_read()` removes the version first. Only IDs of the form `ENSG` (or
`ENSMUSG`, and so on) followed by digits, a dot and digits are changed. Others
are left alone, which is why they end up unannotated (section 6):

```{r}
lookup(c("ENSG00000141510", "ENSG00000182378.14_PAR_Y", "ERCC-00002", "10904"))
```

The version is used only for the lookup. If two files disagreed on a gene's
version, that would already have stopped the run at step 1, because the
`gene_id` values differ.

## 4. One symbol per Ensembl ID

An Ensembl ID can map to several records in the OrgDb. The function keeps the
symbol of the record with the **lowest Entrez ID**, so the choice is fixed and
repeatable.

```{r}
all_ids <- AnnotationDbi::keys(org.Hs.eg.db, "ENSEMBL")
map <- suppressMessages(AnnotationDbi::select(
  org.Hs.eg.db, keys = all_ids, keytype = "ENSEMBL", columns = c("SYMBOL", "ENTREZID")
))
map <- map[!is.na(map$SYMBOL), ]
n_symbols <- tapply(map$SYMBOL, map$ENSEMBL, function(x) length(unique(x)))
c(ensembl_ids_with_symbol = length(n_symbols),
  with_more_than_one_symbol = sum(n_symbols > 1))
```

## 5. Rows that share a symbol are added

The opposite also happens: different Ensembl IDs can carry the same symbol.

```{r}
first <- map[order(map$ENSEMBL, as.numeric(map$ENTREZID)), ]
first <- first[!duplicated(first$ENSEMBL), ]
per_symbol <- table(first$SYMBOL)
c(symbols = length(per_symbol),
  symbols_used_by_several_ids = sum(per_symbol > 1),
  ids_involved = sum(per_symbol[per_symbol > 1]))
```

A table with a row name that appears twice cannot be indexed by name, so these
rows have to be combined. `rsem_read()` **adds** them, for counts and for TPM.
Both are additive quantities: the counts of two gene models are the counts of
the pooled gene, and TPM is a proportion of the library that sums over genes.
Taking the mean or the maximum would make the column totals no longer match the
file.

## 6. Genes without a symbol keep their ID

Some genes have no symbol in the OrgDb: spike-ins, numeric IDs, IDs ending in
`_PAR_Y`, and Ensembl IDs that the OrgDb does not cover. Dropping them would be
simple, but it would also remove their counts. So they stay in the table **under the
`gene_id` written in your file**, version and all, and the column sums remain
equal to the input.

If you want only annotated genes, select the rows that do not look like IDs:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
annotated <- df[!grepl("^ENS", rownames(df)), ]
```

(Adapt the pattern to the IDs in your data; spike-in names are not Ensembl
IDs.)

One more safety rule: if a kept `gene_id` is identical to a gene symbol, the
function stops rather than adding the two rows together.

## 7. What you get

* A data frame; row names are symbols (or kept IDs), column names are
  `sample_id`.
* Rows appear in the order in which they first occur in the files; columns
  follow `metadata.csv`.
* Values are **not rounded** and TPM is **not renormalized**.
* A message gives the numbers of samples, genes, rows, genes with a symbol,
  merged symbols and kept IDs, with the version of the OrgDb package. Use
  `suppressMessages()` to hide it.

Because symbols come from the installed OrgDb, a newer OrgDb can change which
symbols exist or which IDs share them. Note the version in the message when you
report your results.

## What the function does not do

It does not normalize, filter low counts, remove samples, test for differential
expression, round counts, or write files. It also does not support species
other than human and mouse, or gzip-compressed RSEM files.
